issue.title: Recognize glossary terms that wrap across a line break
issue.description: A multiword glossary term stays recognized when a line break falls between its words, so it is highlighted, previewable, and jumpable in ACE and in LSP-backed editors exactly as it is when it fits on one line.

issue.title: Match phrases across one line break and expose per-line span segments
issue.description: core: allow a single line break inside a multiword alias in the Rust matcher, add core-computed per-line display segments to the glossary span wire, and emit one LSP semantic token per segment.

issue.title: Publish a sase-core-rs release containing the matcher change
issue.description: core-release: land the release-plz version bump for sase-core, record the published version, and confirm the wheel resolves from PyPI.

issue.title: Consume segments in ACE, guard the floor, and correct the docs
issue.description: python: move the sase-core-rs window, carry span segments through the facade into the prompt highlight map, normalize wrapped matched text in the preview card, add a published-minimum smoke gate, and fix the docs that promise line-local matching.

payload.entry: Implemented core matcher segments and LSP token splitting; verified just install, just rust-fmt, just rust-check, cargo test --workspace glossary, and cargo test --workspace all pass.

Published version: sase-core-rs==0.22.0 (release-plz PR sase-org/sase-core#101, merged 2026-08-09T20:39:29Z, tag v0.22.0, commit 69c0512). CHANGELOG for crates/sase_core confirms the glossary matcher change (feat(glossary): match phrases across line breaks, commit 4012af5) shipped in this release, alongside the pre-existing breaking change (drop legacy top-level glossary path from glossary_scope_paths) that forced the minor bump from 0.21.3 to 0.22.0 as the epic plan anticipated. Verified 'uv pip install sase-core-rs==0.22.0' resolves from PyPI into a clean venv and that the installed wheel's compile_glossary_catalog().scan() returns the wrapped 'Xprompt Memory' match with two trimmed per-line segments (the reported xprompt/xprompt-memory case). Window shape for the python phase: pyproject.toml sase-core-rs should move to >=0.22.0,<0.23.0 (ceiling widens from <0.22.0 since the published version is 0.22.x, per epic plan Phase 2 step 3). Note: sase-core master has since advanced to v0.23.0 (unrelated breaking change, tale size validation) -- that does not affect this phase's floor, which only needs 0.22.0.

Verified sase-core master carries the core-phase commit (4012af5 feat(glossary): match phrases across line breaks) and that release-plz PR sase-org/sase-core#101 (chore: release v0.22.0, merged 2026-08-09T20:39:29Z) bumped sase_core/sase_core_py to 0.22.0 with a changelog entry covering it, alongside the pre-existing breaking glossary_scope_paths removal -- matching the epic plan's 0.22.x expectation exactly. The Release-plz publish workflow run on commit 69c0512 completed successfully. Confirmed sase-core-rs==0.22.0 resolves and installs from PyPI into a clean venv, and that the installed wheel's compile_glossary_catalog().scan() returns the wrapped 'xprompt\n  memory' text as one Xprompt Memory span with two trimmed single-line segments (reported bug case), not the bare Xprompt term. Recorded the published version and window shape (>=0.22.0,<0.23.0) on this bead via a note for the python phase to consume.
